name: Empathy Gap
description: People in one visceral or emotional state systematically mispredict what they will want, value, or choose in another state. Calm-state planning often fails to anticipate hot-state behavior, and hot-state choices can ignore what seemed sensible when calm.
design_relevance_note: Relevant to commitment devices, cooling-off periods, craving/addiction tools, emergency flows, cancellation/friction debates, and any product where users plan in one state but act in another. The main design lesson is about state mismatch, not generic 'be empathetic' messaging.
prevalence_note: Regularly cited in behavioral-economics, health-behavior, and habit-change product discussions, but not a routine named concept in baseline interface-design teaching.

findings.description: When hunger states at decision time and consumption time were experimentally mismatched, hungry subjects overbid by about 20¢ for a snack they would later eat while satiated, and satiated subjects underbid by about 19¢ for a snack they would later eat while hungry — a direct demonstration that people mispredict preferences across hot/cold visceral states.
findings.effect_size: Hungry subjects overbid by $0.20; satiated subjects underbid by $0.19 under state mismatch
findings.source_title: Symmetry in Cold-to-Hot and Hot-to-Cold Valuation Gaps
